prompt_text: What is the best health insurance broker in Kansas City MO for someone who is self-employed?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” broker for every self‑employed person — the right broker depends on your location, budget, health needs, whether you want an HSA‑eligible plan, and whether you need help with ACA subsidies or small‑group options. I can help you find one, but first here’s a practical way to pick the best broker for you in Kansas City, MO.

Quick guidance and next steps
- Decide what you need: individual/family ACA plan, short‑term, HSA, dental/vision add‑ons, or a small‑group plan if you have employees. Also know your approximate annual income (to check subsidy eligibility).
- Confirm which side of the metro: Missouri and Kansas have different marketplaces and rules. You said Kansas City, MO — good to confirm ZIP code for local broker searches.
- Look for an independent, licensed broker who works with multiple carriers (not captive to a single company). That gives you more plan choices.
- Verify credentials and reputation:
  - Ask to see their Missouri insurance license.
  - Check membership in professional groups (e.g., National Association of Health Underwriters — local chapter).
  - Read Google/Yelp reviews and Better Business Bureau listing.
  - Ask for references from other self‑employed clients.
- Ask these key questions when interviewing a broker:
  - Which carriers and plan types do you represent?
  - Do you specialize in ACA/individual plans and subsidy calculations?
  - Do you charge a broker fee or work on commission?
  - Will you help with enrollment, renewals, and claims issues?
  - How will you handle customer service after enrollment?
- Verify they understand special enrollment periods, tax implications of subsidies, and HSA rules if that matters to you.

Where to search and verify
- Healthcare.gov (or Missouri’s help resources) — use the Marketplace to compare plans and find local agents/brokers certified to enroll people.
- Missouri Department of Commerce & Insurance — to verify a broker’s license and complaints.
- Local NAHU chapter — can refer experienced brokers in KC.
- Consumer review sites (Google, Yelp) and BBB for reputation.

Types of brokers/agencies that often work well for self‑employed people
- Independent, local health insurance brokers who handle ACA plans and small business cases.
- Brokers with experience maximizing Advanced Premium Tax Credit (subsidies) — important if your income fluctuates.
- Agencies that offer ongoing service (renewal help, claims advocacy), not just one‑time enrollment.

If you want, I can:
- Look up and suggest several licensed brokers/agencies in Kansas City, MO (I’ll need your ZIP code or neighborhood).
- Draft a short email/phone script you can use to contact and compare 3–4 brokers.

Which would you like me to do? (If you want local suggestions, please share your ZIP code and whether you need individual/family, HSA, or small‑group coverage.)
